newsitem.title: USA: Mecklenburg Cty, N.C. urged to issue $635 mln GOs.
newsitem.headline: Mecklenburg Cty, N.C. urged to issue $635 mln GOs.

text.p: A citizens committee has proposed that North Carolina's Mecklenburg County issue $635 million of general obligation bonds for capital projects, Finance Director Harry Weatherly said Thursday.
The county can issue $31 million of that without voter approval, and has tentatively schedueld a Nov. 4 referendum on the remaining $604 million.
However, county commissioners have not yet approved the plan, so the amount could change greatly before the referendum.
"It has not been through the normal budget process that will begin at the end of May thorugh the first two weeks of June," Weatherly said.
If the bonds are approved, the first $200 million to $250 milion would be issued between January and March of 1998 and the rest would be issued within 18 months of then.
In addition to the $31 million it can issue without voter approval, the county has $168 million of authorized but unissued debt from previous referendums.
"That's going to be sold next year in January, so I can almost guarantee you $199 million will be sold in that January time frame," Weatherly said.
The bonds would finance school construction and renovation, parks and recreation projects, jails, community college projects and a library.
There would be no impact on property tax rates in fiscal 1998, which begins July 1, and probably none or very little after that, Weatherly said.
"Whether there's a property tax increase depends on the overall spending mix the county will have," he said. "If there is an actual increase, it will be a minimal increase."

The bonds will probably be sold via competitive bid through the North Carolina Division of State and Local Government Finance. But if the bonds are variable rate, the county could consider a negotiated deal, Weatherly said.
